blocks.title: Debugging and bugs
blocks.text: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing bugs, the errors or mistakes in software that cause it to behave unexpectedly. Identifying a bug means observing the software's behaviour and finding the source of the problem; solving it means changing the code to correct the error.

items: Debuggers: software tools that let programmers step through code, inspect variables and monitor program execution.
Print statements: printing the values of variables at different points in the program.
Code reviews: other developers read your code to spot possible errors.

blocks.text: Debugging was named after an incident in 1947 when a real bug, a moth, was found in a computer (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Name three tools or practices for debugging.
blocks.explanation: Debuggers (stepping through code and inspecting variables), print statements (showing variable values) and code reviews (others reading the code).

items: Debugging: finding and fixing bugs; identify by observing behaviour, solve by changing the code.
Tools and practices: debuggers, print statements, code reviews; the name comes from a moth found in 1947.
